meta.title: Example Squad — 2026
meta.note: Delete this file once you have a roadmap of your own. Every field here is editable in Squad Settings — nothing needs hand-editing.

vision: A one-line statement of where this squad is trying to get to. Shown under the title.
problemStatement: What is actually in the way today. Kept separate from the vision so the plan can be argued against the problem rather than against the ambition.

strategicObjectives.name: Reliability
strategicObjectives.description: Make the thing work every time, not just on the happy path.

strategicObjectives.name: Growth
strategicObjectives.description: Unlock the segments the current product cannot serve.

strategicObjectives.name: Platform
strategicObjectives.description: Pay down what makes every other initiative slower than it should be.

sequencing.label: Now
sequencing.text: What is in flight this quarter, and why it is first.

sequencing.label: Next
sequencing.text: What follows, and what has to land before it can start.

sequencing.label: Later
sequencing.text: Named so it stops being re-litigated every planning session.

initiatives.name: An initiative that already shipped
initiatives.description: Initiatives group by objective. Build and rollout are tracked separately because shipping code and turning it on for everyone are different days.

initiatives.name: An initiative in flight
initiatives.description: Set impact from the vocabulary rather than typing it, so it can be weighed against effort.

initiatives.name: An initiative nobody has sized yet
initiatives.description: Impact is deliberately unset here. It renders as nothing rather than as a low priority — an unsized initiative is not the same as an unimportant one.
initiatives.impactNote: Free-text rationale lives here, alongside the picked level.
